newsitem.title: JAPAN: Some Japan local govts halt deals with DKB--paper.
newsitem.headline: Some Japan local govts halt deals with DKB--paper.

text.p: An increasing number of Japanese local governments are cancelling some of their business dealings with Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) due to the bank's suspect loans to racketeers, a business daily said on Tuesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said local governments may take more severe measures against the bank depending on future developments in the case.

Three prefectural governments -- Yamagata in northern Japan, Oita in western Japan, and Tochigi near Tokyo -- as well as two cities have withdrawn some or all of their deposits from DKB, the paper said.
The Tokyo metropolitan government may not include DKB in a syndication group for its bonds to be issued in July, the paper said.
DKB was not immediately available for comment.

Last week, the Finance Ministry said in a report presented to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party that DKB had extended loans of 27.5 billion yen to Yoshinori Koike and his company, part of which was used to to buy shares in Japan's top four securities houses.
Koike and his brother Ryuichi Koike were arrested last mnoth on suspicion of taking about 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
